nodes.action: Read the existing implementation, input shape, documented rules, side-effect behavior, and required return contract.
nodes.name: Inspect project contract
preconditions: Target project and input batch are available
nodes.validator: Rules and output requirements are identified without changing unrelated project structure.

nodes.action: Implement a reusable validator that checks every applicable field, collects all failures for one item, and emits the required structured error shape.
nodes.name: Define local validation
nodes.validator: Invalid items produce all applicable field-level errors before any outbound or mutating call.

nodes.action: Load the batch and process entries in original order while preserving each entry's zero-based index and original payload where required.
nodes.name: Iterate through batch
nodes.validator: Every input entry is examined exactly once and order/index metadata is preserved.

nodes.action: Append a structured failure record for each invalid entry and continue processing subsequent entries.
nodes.name: Record rejected entries
nodes.validator: Failure records contain the contractually required index, original data, and complete errors; invalid entries cause no side effect.

nodes.action: Invoke the existing outbound or mutation operation only for valid entries and collect successful results.
nodes.name: Dispatch valid entries
nodes.validator: No invalid entry reaches the external API or creation operation.

nodes.action: Build the required summary/result object, then verify counts, error shapes, ordering, and absence of forbidden calls.
nodes.name: Assemble and verify result
nodes.validator: Returned keys, counts, traces, and nested records satisfy the documented contract and valid/invalid dispatch invariant.

nodes.action: Read the batch and identify required fields, optional fields, normalization rules, and output/error schemas.
nodes.name: Load and inspect batch contract
preconditions: Input batch and project contract are available
nodes.validator: Records are retained in original order and policy requirements are explicit.

nodes.action: Convert each raw record into a validation-ready representation while preserving its original index and payload.
nodes.name: Project records for validation
nodes.validator: Every candidate has its original zero-based index and source payload.

nodes.action: Validate every candidate before dispatch, applying type, presence, range, enum, format, uniqueness, timezone, and cross-field rules as applicable; collect all failures for each record.
nodes.name: Accumulate local validation errors
nodes.validator: Rejected records contain field/parameter-specific error objects with the required fields, and no candidate is dispatched during validation.

nodes.action: Send only candidates with no validation errors to the external operation, preserving batch order and recording the operation trace.
nodes.name: Dispatch valid candidates
nodes.validator: The number of outbound calls equals the number of valid candidates and invalid candidates cause zero calls.

nodes.action: Build the required structured return value with successes, failures or rejections, counts, original indices/payloads where required, and trace information.
nodes.name: Assemble batch result
nodes.validator: Summary counts reconcile with total input, successes, and failures; all rejected records retain required structured diagnostics.
